subject: Slate model onboarding - pin request + roadmap implications
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Slate model onboarding - pin request + roadmap implications

Hi team,

Quick heads-up: Slate AI wants us to onboard their embargoed 'Slate-XL' variant for downstream customers next week. They are asking us to pin the variant (model: slate-xl-v2) to a fixed serving binary for 60 days while they validate logits stability with their internal evals. Procurement looped me in for a short SLA + pricing conversation; they included a draft SLA and a compatibility matrix (attached).

Asks:
- Dev: can we support a variant pin for slate-xl-v2 without breaking autoscaling or preemptible policies? Any obvious perf regressions we should flag?
- Laura (Product): what are the rollout constraints on the roadmap if we keep a 60-day serve pin? Does this block upcoming multi-model batching changes?
- Monica (Legal/CS): procurement wants standard infra SLAs plus a clause for emergency rollback if safety regressions are found — any redlines we should expect?

I've attached the compatibility spreadsheet and their draft SLA. Procurement is pushing for a >April 8 launch. If we can't meet that timeline, we'll propose a staged canary.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product - Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slate model onboarding - pin request + roadmap implications

Karthik —

Quick read of the matrix: slate-xl-v2 is quantized as int8, KV cache looks standard. Two preliminary notes:
1) Pinning at the serving layer is feasible, but we need to carve out a dedicated variant slot to avoid preemption. That increases cost ~12% for the reserved capacity during the pin window.
2) Multi-model batching change (ETA mid-Apr) will modify scheduling heuristics; if we pin this variant it will be excluded from some cross-model microbatching optimizations until we add whitelist support.

I can prototype a pin toggle today and run a 2-hour soak on staging. If acceptable, I recommend: pin + canary in us-west for 48 hours, then gradual region rollout.

Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@slate.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Slate model onboarding - pin request + roadmap implications

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from procurement:
- The 60-day pin is a hard ask for their compliance window; they can accept a staged canary if the canary schedule is committed in writing.
- SLATE will sign a 30-day service credit cap if there is an incident attributable to our serving variant, but they want the rollback clause to be explicit (we revert to slate-xl-v1 if logits drift > 0.4 on their eval set).

Attached is a redline-friendly SLA. Also, procurement wants to confirm if pinning impacts price tiers (we'd like to know estimated delta and a one-line justification).

Ellen Park
Head of Integrations, Slate AI
E: ellen.park@slate.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slate model onboarding - pin request + roadmap implications

Team —

From a product roadmapping perspective:
- The pin will delay inclusion in the multi-model batching launch for this variant; that's fine from a customer SL perspective if we keep the pin 60 days. The risk is increased unit costs for Slate and slightly worse P50 latency for pinned hosts in the first week.
- Proposed approach: accept the 60-day pin but require a firm canary schedule (2-day us-west canary starting Apr 8, followed by us-east/ap-south on Apr 10/12). We should attach performance guardrails (P50 < 140ms, error rate < 0.5%).

I'll draft the customer-facing rollout plan. Dev, can you confirm the estimated cost delta and whether we can automate rollback on the metric threshold Ellen mentions?

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management - Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Slate model onboarding - pin request + roadmap implications

All —

Legal/CS quick note on the SLA redlines: we can accept the rollback clause as written but need two edits before countersign:
1) Limit the service-credit cap to 30 days of usage (we can set a dollar cap in the SLA).
2) Add a clause that requires Slate to provide their eval set and drift calculations within 24 hours of a claimed regression so we can validate.

Also, procurement/finance will need a short justification for the 12% reserved-cost uplift Dev called out. Suggested one-liner for finance: 'Dedicated variant pin requires reserved host capacity to avoid preemption, which increases committed GPU hours for the pinned variant.'

I'll send a redlined SLA back to Ellen if you all agree. If we keep the Apr 8 canary start, we need engineering sign-off on Monday (Apr 4).

-Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Success & Contracts
Redwood Inference
